meeting_header:
Date: 2025-12-05 | Start: 16:00 PST | Duration: 58m
Redwood: Alex Chen (AE), Priya Rao (SE), Samira Lopez (CSM), Jordan Kim (Legal)
Zenatek: Marta Alvarez (Procurement), Derek Shaw (Legal), Lena Ortiz (CTO), Omar Velez (Security), Noah Park (Finance)
summary: Procurement/gate call to validate MSA/DPA terms, SLA expectations, required security artifacts (SOC2, pentest), onboarding timeline, PO and pricing approval path. Customer requested redlines, encryption/KMS clarifications, and a clear order form + PO process. Redwood agreed to deliver documents and schedule a short technical follow-up around dedicated/private deployment details for security review.
topics: Pricing approvals and reserved capacity discounts
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We know this is the vendor gating call for Zenatek, so goal today is to surface any legal/procurement blockers and agree next steps. I can do a 5 minute intro, then Jordan will cover the MSA/DPA posture, Priya will cover infra/SLAs, and we can go into Q&A.
[00:22] Marta Alvarez: Thanks Alex, appreciate it. We have Derek from legal and Omar from security on the line. I'll run through the procurement gating list if that's ok. We've got a few specific questions on data residency and who manages keys.
[00:36] Alex Chen: Totally, that matches what we were expecting. Jordan, do you want to kick off with the MSA/DPA status?
[00:45] Jordan Kim: Sure. We circulated the latest MSA on Monday — it's the standard Redwood master services agreement with the usual redline track changes. On DPA, we generally offer standard EU/US clauses, addendum for data processing, and options for KMS integration. Note: our DPA notes the ability to support customer-managed keys in certain Private deployments, but that requires additional on-prem or VPC setup.
[01:12] Derek Shaw: Clarify that — "customer-managed keys" means you hold the HSM or we bring a key into your KMS? We need to confirm the separation of duties for encryption.
[01:25] Jordan Kim: Good question. For Hosted API, keys are managed by Redwood unless you choose a Private deployment where we can provide a KMS integration pattern (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and you control key rotation. The on-prem package can also support HSMs.
[01:40] Omar Velez: Right — from security we'll need the KMS integration docs and any architecture diagrams showing key handling. Also need the pen test report redacted if necessary.
[01:52] Priya Rao: We'll attach the KMS integration notes and a deployment diagram. For clarity, Dedicated (Reserved) is a managed pool with tenant isolation; Private (VPC or on-prem) is where you get customer-managed keys and tighter network controls.
[02:08] Lena Ortiz: From a technical perspective, our main questions are latency targets and SLA credits. We're running near-real-time features so 99th percentile is pretty important.
[02:20] Priya Rao: Understood. Our standard hosted SLA is 99.5 uptime for API availability; for Dedicated we can negotiate tighter latency-based SLOs and a credit table. We commonly see customers choose a Reserved Capacity commit to get predictable throughput and a discount. I can send a model for how the credit calculations work.
[02:40] Noah Park: On the finance side, we need to know whether we can put Redwood into our vendor master and what the PO terms look like. Do you accept Net30 or do you require upfront payment for reserved capacity?
[02:54] Alex Chen: We accept Net30 for many enterprise customers; for Reserved Capacity there are options — monthly billing vs annual prepay — we can be flexible depending on contracting. We'll confirm that in the order form we send.
[03:06] Marta Alvarez: Ok. On MSA redlines: we have one clause around indemnity and one on data breach notification time that our legal team wants tweaked. Derek will call those out.
[03:18] Derek Shaw: The breach notification window — can you confirm it's 72 hours in your DPA? Our procurement policy expects 48 hours for critical incidents.
[03:28] Jordan Kim: Our standard is 72 hours; we can take a look but 48 is often a tough ask for large infra investigations. That said, Jordan (Redwood legal) will highlight if we can accelerate for critical severity and include interim notification commitments.
[03:45] Derek Shaw: If you can do an interim notification within 24 hours with a full report by 72, that might be workable.
[03:53] Jordan Kim: We'll propose interim updates and make the communication plan explicit. I'll send suggested language.
[04:00] [00:04:00] Marta Alvarez: Another procurement item — we need SOC2 Type II attestation and the last 12-months pen test exec summary. Are these ready?
[04:12] Jordan Kim: Yes, SOC2 report is current to 2025 Q3. I can send the report under NDA if you need the full copy and a redacted exec summary publicly. We also have a summary of the external penetration test; full details are sensitive but we can provide an exec summary and remediation timeline.
[04:28] Omar Velez: We'll want evidence of encryption at rest and in transit, KV cache handling, and any potential exfiltration vectors — sometimes transcripts show up in logs, we need to confirm retention.
[04:42] Priya Rao: Good point on retention. For Hosted, logs and debug traces used for troubleshooting are retained for a short window by default, and customers can opt-in for longer retention via the Console. We can also enable customer-only retention in Private deployments. We'll document the retention policy and retention-change process.
[05:00] Lena Ortiz: About model outputs — we need assurances on data use. Are generated outputs used to train models?
[05:10] Alex Chen: Redwood's standard position is we do not use customer prompts or outputs to retrain models unless explicitly agreed. That is part of the DPA language and the data usage section — we'll include that clause in the DPA copy.
[05:20] Derek Shaw: Great. On SLA credit language, we need a deterministic credit table for outages and latency misses. We also need a path for dispute resolution — arbitration clause and jurisdiction.
[05:34] Jordan Kim: The MSA contains our arbitration and jurisdiction defaults but we're open to limited modifications for enterprise deals. For the credit table I'll put our standard table and a sample calculation for a missed 99th percentile latency SLO for reserved capacity.
[05:50] Marta Alvarez: Procurement will need a single order form that lists the PO number, billing contact, and detailed list of SKUs and seat/throughput numbers. Noah, can you confirm your internal process?
[06:01] Noah Park: We require vendor code and an initial vendor risk score. If legal clears MSA/DPA and security gets the SOC2 + pen test, we can usually do a standard PO within 7 business days. For discounts on reserved capacity, procurement needs a signed order form and internal budget approval.
[06:17] Alex Chen: We'll supply a clean order form and a redline-ready copy for your legal. We'll also provide a pricing worksheet that shows baseline vs reserved capacity discounts and cushion options.
[06:28] [00:06:28] Priya Rao: Quick note on deployment: if you want customer-managed keys and private networking, that tends to push us to the Private deployment model. There are two options: VPC-private with managed control plane, or fully on-prem. Both require additional onboarding steps and lead time for network peering and firewall rules.
[06:46] Omar Velez: If we go VPC-private, we'll need flow logs and an ingress/egress allowlist. Also want to confirm whether Redwood personnel require jumpbox access during onboarding.
[06:58] Priya Rao: Typically we use temporary bastion access tied to a scoped SRE runbook; long-term access is not required. We'll document the least-privilege onboarding approach.
[07:08] Derek Shaw: A few legal redline asks: 1) Limitations on consequential damages — can we carve out cap for intellectual property claims? 2) More explicit data handling for sub-processors.
[07:21] Jordan Kim: We can discuss both. For consequential damages, our standard cap is tied to fees paid in the previous 12 months; we can consider tweaks in enterprise buy. For sub-processors we already have a clause listing subprocessors and processes for notice. We'll include a sub-processor list link.
[07:36] Marta Alvarez: On timing — procurement review is scheduled to meet next Friday for vendor gating. If you can get docs to us by Tuesday EOD we can include them in the packet.
[07:47] Alex Chen: That's doable. We'll target Tuesday EOD with the MSA redline copy, DPA, SOC2, pen test exec summary, and order form.
[07:56] [00:07:56] Lena Ortiz: On the pricing side, curious how usage spikes are handled. If we hit a burst over reserved throughput, what's the fallback? Throttling or overflow to hosted?
[08:09] Priya Rao: We have configurable burst capacity options and overflow policies. You can route overflow to a lower-cost model variant or to a higher-capacity pool. We'll include examples in the pricing worksheet. For strict latency guarantees you typically keep cushion in reserved capacity.
[08:24] Noah Park: Also need clarity on tax handling and whether we issue invoices with tax breakdowns.
[08:31] Alex Chen: Yes, the order form includes tax fields and we can include the VAT/sales tax line items where applicable.
[08:38] [00:08:38] Marta Alvarez: Are there any third-party sub-contractors that host customer data aside from cloud providers? We need a list for vendor risk scoring.
[08:48] Jordan Kim: Our primary subprocessors are cloud infra providers (AWS, GCP), CDNs for certain regions, and monitoring vendors; we'll provide a subprocessors list link. We don't use external vendors to train models on customer data.
[08:59] Derek Shaw: One more legal item — termination assistance obligations. We need a clear order for data return/deletion, timelines, and export formats.
[09:10] Jordan Kim: Agreed. Our MSA has a termination assistance section; typical windows are 30 days for export and 90 days for residual deletion unless otherwise negotiated. We can tighten that if required.
[09:23] Alex Chen: Alright, maybe let's surface the high-risk blockers now. Derek?
[09:28] Derek Shaw: High risk: breach notification timeline, KMS tenancy control, and termination assistance windows. Medium risk: SLA credits wording and jurisdiction. Low risk: tax breakdown and PO fields.
[09:42] Priya Rao: For each high risk, we can propose mitigations: interim notification language + full report by 72 hours; customer-managed KMS in Private deployments; and 30/90 termination assistance with optional tighter SLAs for enterprise.
[09:56] Marta Alvarez: That helps. Procurement needs to see proposed language for the notification and the KMS integration checklist.
[10:05] Alex Chen: We'll include those. Jordan will drop the legal language, Priya will drop the tech diagram and KMS checklist, and Samira will include the onboarding checklist and contact matrix.
[10:15] [00:10:15] Omar Velez: One technical nit: you mentioned "KV cache handling" earlier — can you confirm whether any ephemeral caches ever persist to disk or logs? We need assurance there are no long-term caches that could hold prompt data.
[10:29] Priya Rao: The runtime uses in-memory KV caches for decoding fast paths. We don't persist KV caches to long-term disk in standard hosted or dedicated modes. For Private, there are configurable cache persistence options but those require explicit setup. We'll document the default behavior.
[10:43] Lena Ortiz: Good. Also please include an attachable runbook for incident response and contact SLAs.
[10:50] Jordan Kim: We'll include an IR runbook summary.
[10:54] Alex Chen: Any questions on pricing or discounts before we round?
[10:58] Noah Park: Just to be clear: could you give a sample discount band for a 12-month reserved commit at 100k tokens/day throughput? We just need a ballpark to consider budget.
[11:10] Priya Rao: I'll include a pricing worksheet with bands. As an example, 12-month commit might get ~20% off list depending on exact throughput and support tier; Reserved also includes prioritization and lower eviction risk.
[11:23] Marta Alvarez: We'll need that in the packet.
[11:26] [00:11:26] Alex Chen: Ok let's go to wrap. We'll recap commitments and timeline. Jordan?
[11:33] Jordan Kim: Commitments: I'll send SOC2 cert and pen test executive summary, and suggested redline language for breach notification and termination assistance.
[11:42] Priya Rao: I'll send the KMS integration doc, topology diagram for VPC-private, and a pricing worksheet with cushion examples.
[11:49] Samira Lopez: I'll include an onboarding checklist and contact matrix and propose the pilot onboarding timeline.
[11:56] Alex Chen: From Redwood we'll get all docs to you by Tuesday EOD so you can make the procurement packet for your Friday gating meeting.
[12:04] Marta Alvarez: Sounds good. Any final clarifying Qs?
[12:08] Derek Shaw: No further questions. We'll review the redlines once received.
[12:12] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[12:15] Alex Chen: Thanks all, talk soon.
[12:18] [End of transcript]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings (K V cache, RedWood capitalization), filler words and overlaps. Links referenced during call: [MSA draft link], [DPA link], [SOC2 cert link], [pen test exec summary], [order form template].
